canonical_statement: On a probability space, the forward Cesaro averages of every real integrable observable under a measure-preserving endomorphism converge almost everywhere to an integrable invariant function; if the endomorphism is ergodic, the limit equals the constant space integral almost everywhere.
domain_and_universes: universe u; X : Type u; MeasurableSpace X; probability measure mu; T : X -> X; f,g : X -> Real; Prop in Lean universe 0
conclusion: There exists an integrable g, invariant under T almost everywhere, to which the forward Cesaro iterates converge pointwise almost everywhere; Ergodic T mu implies g is almost everywhere the constant integral of f.
normalization: timeAverage T f n x = (n : Real)^(-1) times the sum over k in range n of f ((T^[k]) x); the value at n=0 is zero and convergence is along atTop

killed: changed probability measure to merely finite measure
substituted L1 mean convergence for pointwise almost-everywhere convergence

degenerate_cases: No invertibility or non-atomicity assumption is imposed. The n=0 average is defined as zero and is irrelevant along atTop. The ergodicity hypothesis is required only for identification with the space integral, not for existence of the invariant limit.
